about.en:
The Leiden Summer School in Languages and Linguistics is one of Europe's best-known summer programmes for linguistics and ancient languages. The 2027 edition runs Monday 5 to Friday 16 July 2027 in Leiden (Netherlands), with tracks in Anatolian, Classics, Descriptive Linguistics, Language Documentation, Eastern Christianity, Germanic, General Linguistics, Historical Linguistics, Indo-European, Indology, Iranian, Papyrology, Russian Literature, Semitic and Sino-Tibetan.

It is open to bachelor, master and PhD students. Courses are taught in English (Russian Literature in Russian) and most are hybrid, so you can also join online. Active participation earns 2 ECTS per course, plus 3 ECTS with an extra take-home assignment.

The full course list is published around February/March 2027, when registration opens; the deadline is 3 May 2027. It is a rare chance to learn rare languages from Leiden specialists alongside students from all over the world.

about.en:
EM Strasbourg Business School's Summer School runs 11–25 June 2027 in Strasbourg, home of the European Parliament and the Council of Europe. The core course, Business in Europe, covers Responsible Leadership for a Sustainable Europe and Understanding Europe, worth 6 ECTS (3 US credits).

Visits have included the European Parliament, the Council of Europe, Mercedes-Benz and Weberhaus, alongside cultural activities (wine tour, cheese tasting, cooking workshop). The fee covers tuition, corporate visits, cultural activities and welcome/farewell lunches; housing in student residences is about €300–350.

Open to undergraduates with at least one year of higher education (business or economics basics) and English B2. Apply by 15 March 2027.

Teams design a game that can be played inside a museum and is accessible to everyone, using 3D scanning and printing, laser cutting, augmented and virtual reality and graphic design tools.

Visits include the Musée de l'École de Nancy and the Centre Pompidou-Metz, with excursions to Metz and the Vosges mountains. Completion earns 3 ECTS and a certificate.

It is open to all students, taught in English, with no prior technical knowledge needed. Registration for 2027 is open now.

It is for female undergraduates or graduates aged 18+ with at least six months of Japanese. Apply 5 January – 18 February 2027.

It is open to undergraduate and graduate students enrolled at an international university with a GPA of at least 2.7; freshmen and sophomores need professor approval before applying.

Apply 2 February – 12 April 2027 (USD 200 application fee).

en: 8 weeks of full-time research
Pick from the 2027 NTU faculty list
Certificate and transcript

eligibility.en: Undergraduate/graduate students at an international university; GPA ≥2.7; freshmen/sophomores need professor approval.

en: Check the 2027 NTU faculty list and contact a potential supervisor.
Apply online 2 Feb – 12 Apr 2027 and pay USD 200.
Pay the programme fee after acceptance.
Arrange visa and housing.

costs.en: USD 200 non-refundable application fee; programme fee (shown on the official page) covers tuition, orientation, cultural courses, activities and accident insurance. Accommodation not included.

about.en:
UTokyo Global Unit Courses (GUC) are short, intensive, English-taught courses at the University of Tokyo, organised in two-week terms across June and July. Students can take in-person or online courses and earn Global Unit Certificates.

GUC is open to full-time undergraduate and graduate students at non-Japanese universities who have completed at least one term, with TOEFL iBT 90 / IELTS 6.5. Partner-network (AUA, IARU, USTEP) students may get 20% off.

Details for GUC 2027 will be posted around the second week of January 2027. For reference, 2026 fees were JPY 190,000 per in-person 1-unit course and JPY 40,000 per online half-unit course, with applications from early February to mid-March.

en: Japan's top university
In-person or online options
20% discount for AUA/IARU/USTEP students

eligibility.en: Full-time undergraduate or graduate students at non-Japanese universities, at least one completed term; TOEFL iBT 90 / IELTS 6.5.

en: Watch the GUC page for 2027 details (around mid-January 2027).
Register on the UTokyo application system (TAO).
Submit transcript, student ID and English score and pay the JPY 5,000 fee.
Pay course fees after selection; arrange your own housing.

costs.en: 2027 fees TBA (2026: JPY 190,000 per in-person 1-unit course, JPY 380,000 for 2-unit, JPY 40,000 online 0.5-unit; JPY 5,000 application fee). No campus housing. FUTI scholarship for US students.

score_reason: Top university; 2027 cycle confirmed, details in January

about.en:
The University of Liverpool International Summer School offers short, credit-bearing academic modules that complement your home degree, plus an English Communication Skills pathway, in the Russell Group university's city-centre campus. A social programme explores Liverpool's culture, and students live in city-centre residences.

It is open to current undergraduate and postgraduate students and recent graduates worldwide aged 18+. Academic modules need IELTS 6.0 (B2) unless your university teaches in English; the English pathway needs IELTS 5.0 (B1). After paying you receive a confirmation for a UK visitor visa, with a refund if the visa is refused.

Applications for Summer 2027 are due to open soon (the 2026 deadline was 1 May); email iss@liverpool.ac.uk to register interest.

en: Russell Group university, credit-bearing
English skills pathway for B1 learners
Visa-refusal refund guarantee

eligibility.en: Current undergraduate/postgraduate students or graduates of any university, aged 18+; IELTS 6.0 for academic modules (5.0 for the English pathway) unless taught in English.

en: Register interest at iss@liverpool.ac.uk.
Apply online when Summer 2027 applications open.
Pay tuition and accommodation.
Use the confirmation letter for a UK visitor visa if needed.

costs.en: 2027 fees on the 'Dates and fees' page when published; discounts for Liverpool/XJTLU students. Accommodation optional.

about.en:
The International Summer Programme is run by the University of Cambridge's continuing-education institute and brings together learners aged 18 to 80+ from around the world. Participants study for one to four weeks (minimum one week), choosing from subject streams and over 140 courses with one or two daily lectures.

You can stay in one of five historic Cambridge colleges with breakfast and dinner included. There are no formal academic entry requirements beyond good English, making it one of the few official Cambridge summer options open to first-year students and recent school-leavers aged 18+.

The 2026 programme has ended and the 2027 programme is being prepared; register interest through the official 2027 enquiry form for dates, fees and bursaries.

en: Official University of Cambridge programme
140+ courses, 1–4 weeks
Live in a historic college

eligibility.en: Adults aged 18+ (no upper limit) with good English; no formal academic prerequisites.

en: Register interest via the official 2027 contact form.
Choose weeks and courses when the 2027 programme is published.
Book online and choose college accommodation if wanted.
Pay fees and arrange a UK visitor visa if needed.

costs.en: 2027 fees and bursary details to be published on the Fees page; college accommodation with breakfast and dinner optional.
